title: Understanding the Expression
text: The expression $y_i-\sigma(X_{i}\cdot{\theta}**{(t)})$ involves a subtraction operation. Let's break it down to understand its components.

title: Components of the Expression
text: In the expression $y_i-\sigma(X_{i}\cdot{\theta}**{(t)})$, $y_i$ is a scalar value representing a single outcome (either $$0$$ or 1).

title: Understanding the Sigma Function
text: The function $\sigma(X_{i}\cdot{\theta}**{(t)})$ is the sigmoid function applied to the dot product of $X_i$ and $\theta**{(t)}$. This results in a scalar value between $$0$$ and $$1$$.

title: Dimensions of the Dot Product
text: The dot product $X_{i}\cdot{\theta}**{(t)}$ results in a scalar because $X_i$ is a row vector and $\theta**{(t)}$ is a column vector.

title: Final Dimension of the Expression
text: Since both $y_i$ and $\sigma(X_{i}\cdot{\theta}**{(t)})$ are scalars, the expression $y_i-\sigma(X_{i}\cdot{\theta}**{(t)})$ is also a scalar.
